The plan cites topaz-blubbery-mice and cranial-goodly-seahog but never mentions restoring-shallow-blobfish, the ticket that actually owns surface-parity and recorded the negative result for the static approach.
topaz's rationale that surface drift was previously 'caught only by chance or by LLM review' — i.e. LLM review was the known-insufficient baseline the oracle was built to replace.
findings.finding: The plan reintroduces a static (LLM review-time) surface-parity check without confronting that the dedicated surface-parity ticket (restoring-shallow-blobfish, named on cranial-goodly-seahog) had its design REVISED AWAY from a signature-introspection/static approach to Pattern A generation, precisely because a parity experiment showed signature-introspection false-positives and a runtime close_class blind spot.
findings.location: Plan 'Add code-review surface-parity criterion' — Approach / Scope; the 'STATIC code-review complement' framing
scenarios: Reviewer fires false positives on adapter-bound param differences the introspection experiment already showed are noise.
The overlay re-treads a design space an existing sibling ticket already explored and moved past, duplicating effort and risking a contradictory second solution to the same concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / why not restoring-shallow-blobfish' note: argue the overlay is a natural-language coach (not signature introspection), cite the false-positive guards as the mitigation for the recorded FP class, and confirm ownership boundaries with that ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Delineate the surface-parity overlay from the existing api-compat overlay (which already covers asymmetric-interface-change and routes **/cli*/**/mcp_server*): justify a new overlay over extending api-compat, or scope-carve so the two do not double-emit on the same write-op diff.
evidence: code-review-api-compat.md: 'asymmetric interface change: one side of an interface contract is updated but not its counterpart — a function signature changes (added/renamed/reordered/removed parameter...) but Grep shows callsites still using the old form.'
criteria_routing.json api-compat applies_to includes '**/cli*' and '**/mcp_server*' — already routing CLI/MCP surface changes to a compat reviewer.
The plan's differentiator (lib/CLI/MCP write-op lockstep) is a narrower special case of api-compat's asymmetric-interface-change class.
findings.finding: The new overlay's concern substantially overlaps the existing api-compat overlay, which already flags 'asymmetric interface change: one side of an interface contract is updated but not its counterpart' and 'producer/consumer drift', and whose applies_to globs already include **/cli* and **/mcp_server* — yet the plan does not delineate why a new overlay is preferable to extending api-compat.
findings.location: Plan Approach step 1 (three write surfaces) / step 3 (new criteria_routing.json entry); criteria_routing.json api-compat entry
scenarios: A write-op param added to one adapter fires BOTH api-compat and surface-parity, producing duplicate/near-duplicate advisories that the Pass-2/3 dedup must absorb.
A future maintainer must reason about which of two overlapping overlays owns a CLI/MCP surface finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach naming api-compat and stating the boundary (e.g. api-compat = public/wire contract compat vs. surface-parity = internal three-adapter lockstep for write ops), and note the Pass-2/3 dedup handles any residual overlap.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Engage the recorded signature-parity experiment on cranial-goodly-seahog / restoring-shallow-blobfish: state explicitly that this STATIC overlay covers only the param/guard/required-field SURFACE (not the runtime conditional-required rule the experiment found it blind to), that the runtime rule is delegated to the topaz oracle, and justify why the static overlay is net-valuable despite the documented false-positive/blind-spot history.
evidence: cranial-goodly-seahog comment: 'surface-parity: design revised to Pattern A (single-source-of-truth + generation) after the parity experiment showed signature-introspection false-positives + a runtime close_class blind spot'

restoring-shallow-blobfish EXPERIMENT comment: 'Contrast the earlier naive signature-parity experiment, which fired on 4/5 ops with FALSE-POSITIVES (force_close/source/return_alias/_creation_channel) and was BLIND to the runtime close_class rule.'

restoring-shallow-blobfish deep-dive G4: 'THE REAL PARITY RISK IS BEHAVIORAL, and generation [and, equally, a static surface check] cannot express it ... A generated surface would look identical yet still diverge on exactly what this ticket cares about -> false confidence.'
Plan Approach step 1: reviewer 'to Grep the sibling adapters for the changed param/guard' — a static param/guard surface signal, the shape the recorded experiment found limited.
findings.finding: The plan revives a STATIC param/guard/required-field surface-parity signal that this ticket's own recorded experiments (on restoring-shallow-blobfish and cited on cranial-goodly-seahog) characterized as limited — the signature-parity prototype produced false-positives and was BLIND to the runtime conditional-required rule (close_class required iff bug-close; reason per REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES). The plan engages only the false-positive half (via its adapter-bound-param guard) and does not acknowledge or bound the recorded runtime blind-spot, nor justify how the static overlay's scope divides against the runtime oracle that was explicitly built to cover it.
findings.location: Plan sections 'Add code-review surface-parity...' intro + 'Approach' step 1 (the Grep-siblings-for-changed-param/guard mechanism)
scenarios: A write-op change alters the RUNTIME conditional-required behavior (e.g. a new REASON_REQUIRED close class) without changing the visible param/guard surface: the static overlay sees lockstep params and stays silent, exactly the G4 blind-spot the recorded experiment flagged — the escaped-bug class this ticket targets can still slip through the static gate.

A reviewer treats a PASS from the static overlay as a parity guarantee, producing the 'false confidence' the deep-dive warned of when the oracle is absent or its rows are xfail'd for a not-yet-landed adapter gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / scope boundary vs the runtime oracle' note to the plan: cite the recorded signature-parity experiment, acknowledge the two documented failure modes (adapter-bound false-positives — mitigated here by the false-positive guard; runtime conditional-required blind-spot — OUT of scope, owned by the topaz oracle), and state that the overlay is an author-time COACH on the visible surface only, not a behavioral-parity guarantee.

The prompt is told to 'enumerate the three write surfaces' — three, matching lib/CLI/MCP, not a fourth 'import-format'
findings.finding: The title says 'CLI <-> MCP <-> import-format lockstep' but the body and Approach consistently name the three write surfaces as lib `_lib_writes.py`, CLI `_commands/`, and MCP `_mcp_writes.py` — 'import-format' never reappears and maps ambiguously to the library/import facade. This is a minor terminology mismatch, not scope drift, but a reader (or the reviewer prompt author) could be confused about whether 'import-format' names a fourth surface or is a synonym for the lib facade.
findings.location: Title: 'Add code-review surface-parity criterion (CLI <-> MCP <-> import-format lockstep)'
scenarios: A reader of the title expects a distinct 'import-format' surface and looks for a fourth adapter that does not exist.
The reviewer-prompt author is unsure whether 'import-format' equals `_lib_writes.py` or a separate concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the title clause to 'CLI <-> MCP <-> library-facade lockstep' (or add a parenthetical in Approach step 1 that 'import-format' = the `_lib_writes.py` library facade).

findings.checklist_item: State the positive rationale distinguishing surface-parity from api-compat (e.g. api-compat's globs never route on the write-adapter files so surface-parity fills a deterministic-triggering gap; plus its required-field/guard scope), so the choice of a separate overlay is defended rather than repackaged.
evidence: code-review-api-compat.md lines 26-29: 'asymmetric interface change: one side of an interface contract is updated but not its counterpart — a function signature changes (added/renamed/reordered/removed parameter, changed return shape) but Grep shows callsites still using the old form.'

The plan targets 'when a write-op's parameter / guard / required-field surface changes on ONE adapter ... without the sibling surfaces being updated in lockstep' — an adapter-to-sibling asymmetric-interface case api-compat's rubric already covers.

The actual distinguishing fact IS available but unstated: api-compat's criteria_routing.json applies_to globs (`**/*api*`, `**/schemas/**`, `**/*.proto`, `**/cli*`, `**/mcp_server*`) do NOT match `_lib_writes.py`, `_commands/transition.py`, or `_mcp_writes.py`, so api-compat never deterministically glob-fires on write-adapter diffs — surface-parity fills that routing gap. Absent from the plan, this is a missing positive rationale under G6(4).
findings.finding: The plan does not state a positive rationale distinguishing the new surface-parity overlay from the existing api-compat overlay, which already detects the same 'asymmetric interface change' defect class (a param/signature changed on one side while the counterpart still uses the old form). The plan models ON api-compat but never says why api-compat is insufficient for the write-adapter case, so the choice to mint a separate overlay is not defended against the obvious reuse/extend alternative.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Model it on the existing GLOB-triggered overlays (api-compat, security)'
scenarios: A diff adds a `reason` param to `_lib_writes.py` but not `_mcp_writes.py` and the base reviewer escalates api-compat: both api-compat and surface-parity fire, producing overlapping findings on the same change — a reviewer/implementer cannot tell from the plan why both are wanted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one or two sentences to the Approach section noting that api-compat's applies_to globs (**/*api*, **/schemas/**, **/*.proto, **/cli*, **/mcp_server*) do NOT match the write-adapter paths, so api-compat only fires on those diffs via base-reviewer escalation, whereas surface-parity glob-triggers deterministically on the three adapters and additionally covers required-field/guard lockstep that api-compat's signature-focused rubric does not target.
